title: Recognize and phrase each JTBD step through its step's slotted templates

facts.note: Contextual hint only: the planner task mentions recognizing, classifying, reviewing, authoring or rewording JTBD steps / WMBTs / acceptances. Keywords alone are not a sufficient trigger.
Planning artifacts in which JTBD step statements live (read or written).

Whether the planner is recognizing/classifying a step statement (including existing, unchanged ones) or authoring/rewording one is judged from the task and the planner's output; no tool observer exists.

Needs a diff-level observer extracting step/WMBT statement text and declared step from planning artifacts. Not required for recognition of unchanged statements, which is covered by the operation fact.

values: step phrasing does not match any template of its step
facts.note: implementation.type is none: no mechanical detector; matching surface grammar to templates is judged by an LLM/reviewer.

fires: Planner classifies an existing, unchanged statement into one of the nine JTBD steps (define, locate, prepare, confirm, execute, monitor, modify, resolve, conclude) by recognizing its template.
Planner reviews existing step statements in a plan/wagon/WMBT for conformance, even when no text is changed.
Planner writes a new WMBT/step statement under one of the nine JTBD steps.
Planner rewords an existing step statement or reclassifies it to another step.
Planner derives acceptances from a step statement whose step must first be recognized from its phrasing.
doesNotFire: Work on planning prose that is not a JTBD step statement (e.g. background notes, rationale) and involves no step classification.
Work that neither recognizes/classifies JTBD step statements nor authors/rewords them (e.g. implementation edits that never consult a step statement).

given: A planning artifact contains, or is to contain, a JTBD job-step statement
when: The planner recognizes/classifies that statement's step, or writes or rewords it
then: Recognize and phrase the statement through one of the fixed slotted templates of a single step: its template determines its step, and its slots bind the step verb to concrete objects, constraints or outcomes.
prefer: define: Define {object} as {specification}; Plan {approach} for {outcome}; Select {option} from {alternatives}; Determine {criteria} for {decision}
locate: Locate {resource} within {constraint}; Gather {inputs} from {sources}; Access {data} via {method}; Retrieve {information} in {timeframe}
prepare: Prepare {environment} for {activity}; Set up {infrastructure} with {configuration}; Organize {resources} by {criteria}; Examine {inputs} for {validation}
confirm: Confirm {precondition} before {action}; Validate {input} against {criteria}; Prioritize {items} by {importance}; Decide {path} based on {conditions}
execute: Execute {action} within {constraint}; Perform {operation} on {target}; Transact {change} to {system}; Administer {process} per {protocol}
monitor: Monitor {metric} for {threshold}; Verify {state} remains {condition}; Track {progress} against {target}; Check {status} every {interval}
modify: Modify {parameter} when {condition}; Update {configuration} to {value}; Adjust {setting} for {optimization}; Maintain {state} within {bounds}
resolve: Resolve {issue} using {method}; Troubleshoot {problem} via {diagnosis}; Fix {error} within {timeframe}; Handle {exception} with {fallback}
conclude: Conclude {job} with {summary}; Store {results} in {location}; Finish {process} by {action}; Close {session} after {cleanup}
avoid: Vague, unslotted phrasing such as "Do the thing with the stuff".
Classifying a statement into a step whose templates it does not match, or using another step's template.
Filling slots with placeholders or vague nouns just to match the template surface.
why: Templated phrasings make step classification and acceptance authoring deterministic — the same surface grammar always maps to the same step.
evidence: Each step statement's leading verb and slot structure match one of the four templates listed for its classified step.
Positive examples: "Define {object} as {specification}", "Monitor {metric} for {threshold}"; negative example: "Do the thing with the stuff".
Reviewer can re-derive the step classification from the phrasing alone and it equals the declared step.
verifier_detail: Term patterns_by_step: per-step linguistic templates with slot placeholders for objects, constraints, and outcomes; 9 steps x 4 templates (see prefer[0..8]).
Statement: each JTBD step is recognized and phrased through a fixed set of slotted linguistic templates that bind the step's verb to its objects and constraints.
Content examples called out in source: "Execute {action} within {constraint}", "Resolve {issue} using {method}".
implementation.type is none: no mechanical detector; compliance is judged by review/LLM.
Step names are those of planner.steps.jtbd-taxonomy (patterns are defined per step name).

additions.justification: Metric-gaming guard required by the schema; the negative example shows vague objects defeat the purpose.

additions.justification: Operationalises the source summary (deterministic classification) as a review check.
All 36 per-step templates are decision-relevant for the planner (both for recognizing and phrasing steps) and are kept in prefer for losslessness.
